inhalt: Cotton uses a lot of water
Polyester is a synthetic fabric derived from petroleum. It is not biodegradable and can take hundreds of years to decompose.
Polyester releases microplastics into water systems every time it is washed. These microplastics harm marine life and enter the food chain.
The production of polyester requires large amounts of energy and generates significant CO2 emissions.
Conventional cotton farming uses approximately 2,700 liters of water to produce one cotton t-shirt.
